def-temperley-lieb-quantum-integers-and-:
## Definition

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit and $\delta\in R$. Define the quantum integers by

$$[0]_\delta=0,\qquad [1]_\delta=1,\qquad [r+1]_\delta=\delta[r]_\delta-[r-1]_\delta\quad(r\ge1).$$

The **quantum characteristic** of $(R,\delta)$ is the least positive integer $\ell$ with $[\ell]_\delta=0$, if one exists, and $\ell=\infty$ otherwise. No element of $R$ is inverted in this definition.

For $q\in\mathbb C^\times$ and $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, write $[r]_q=[r]_\delta$. If $q\ne\pm1$, this agrees with $(q^r-q^{-r})/(q-q^{-1})$; at $q=\pm1$ the recurrence gives $[r]_q=rq^{r-1}$. For complex-parameter classification, write $\kappa=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)$, with $\kappa=\infty$ when $q^2$ has infinite order. If $q\ne\pm1$, the quantum characteristic equals $\kappa$ when $\kappa<\infty$ and is $\infty$ otherwise. At $q=\pm1$, $\kappa=1$ but the complex quantum characteristic is $\infty$, because $[r]_q=rq^{r-1}\ne0$ for every positive $r$.

For a field $K$ of positive characteristic $p$, set $p(0)=1$ and, when $\ell<\infty$, set $p(i)=\ell p^{i-1}$ for $i\ge1$. In characteristic zero and finite $\ell$, the finite digit scale is $p(1)=\ell$; the separate characteristic-zero criterion below uses $a\ell-1$ for arbitrary positive integers $a$. If $\ell=\infty$, every finite index is already in the range $n<\ell$.
lem-temperley-lieb-link-state-gram-deter:
## Statement

Let $q\in\mathbb C^\times$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, $n\ge0$, and $0\le p\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. Put $t=n-2p$, and let $G_{n,p}$ be the Gram matrix of the link-state form on $W_{n,t}(\mathbb C,\delta)$ in its link-state basis. Set

$$d_{n,r}=\binom nr-\binom n{r-1},\qquad \binom n{-1}=0.$$

Then

$$\det G_{n,p}=\prod_{j=1}^{p}\left(\frac{[n-2p+1+j]_q}{[j]_q}\right)^{d_{n,p-j}}.$$

The empty product for $p=0$ is $1$. The right side is interpreted as its polynomial continuation in $\delta$ at parameter values where an individual displayed quotient has a removable zero-over-zero form.
lem-temperley-lieb-cell-forms-detect-sem:
## Statement

For every $n\ge0$, the complex algebra $\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ is semisimple if and only if every link-state cell form $\phi_{n,t}$ is nondegenerate.
def-temperley-lieb-normalized-markov-tra:
## Definition

Let $\delta\in\mathbb C^\times$. For a basis diagram $D:n\to n$ in [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]], join each top boundary point to the corresponding bottom boundary point outside the rectangle. Let $c(D)$ be the number of closed components of this finite matching graph. Define the normalized closure trace on the diagram basis by

$$\tau_n(D)=\delta^{c(D)-n},$$

and extend $\mathbb C$-linearly to $\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$. In particular, $\tau_n(1_n)=1$.
lem-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-is-cycl:
## Statement

For $\delta\in\mathbb C^\times$, the maps $\tau_n$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-normalized-markov-trace-by-closure]] satisfy

$$\tau_n(xy)=\tau_n(yx),\qquad \tau_{n+1}(x\otimes1)=\tau_n(x),\qquad \tau_{n+1}((x\otimes1)d_n)=\delta^{-1}\tau_n(x)$$

for every $n\ge0$ and $x,y\in\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ in the first two identities, and for every $n\ge1$ and $x\in\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ in the third identity, where $d_n$ is the elementary cup-cap diagram on the last two strands.
def-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-recursion:
## Definition

Let $\delta\in\mathbb C$ and use the quantum integers of [[def-temperley-lieb-quantum-integers-and-quantum-characteristic]]. Define $p_0=1\in\mathrm{TL}_0$ and $p_1=1\in\mathrm{TL}_1$. If $[2]_\delta,\ldots,[n]_\delta$ are nonzero, define recursively, for $1\le r<n$,

$$P_r=p_r\otimes1\in\mathrm{TL}_{r+1},\qquad p_{r+1}=P_r-\frac{[r]_\delta}{[r+1]_\delta}P_r d_r P_r.$$

The element $p_n$ defined by this recursion is the Jones–Wenzl element in the nonvanishing-denominator range. This definition makes no assertion that failure of the displayed recursion implies nonexistence of any idempotent.
lem-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-recursion:
## Statement

Let $\delta\in\mathbb C^\times$ and suppose $[2]_\delta,\ldots,[n]_\delta$ are nonzero. The recursively defined $p_n$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-recursion]] is nonzero, satisfies $p_n^2=p_n$, and obeys $d_i p_n=p_n d_i=0$ for $1\le i<n$. Its corner is one-dimensional, $p_n\mathrm{TL}_n p_n=\mathbb C p_n$, and its normalized closure trace is

$$\tau_n(p_n)=\frac{[n+1]_\delta}{\delta^n}.$$
thm-temperley-lieb-trace-degenerates-at-:
## Statement

Let $q^2$ have finite order $\ell\ge3$, put $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, and let $n=\ell-1$. Then $\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ is semisimple but the bilinear trace form $(x,y)\mapsto\tau_n(xy)$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-normalized-markov-trace-by-closure]] is degenerate.
lem-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-projector:
## Statement

Let $K$ be a field, $\delta\in K$, $n\ge0$, and $A=\mathrm{TL}_n(K,\delta)$. Let $\varepsilon:A\to K$ send the identity diagram to $1$ and every nonidentity basis diagram to $0$. Let $K_\varepsilon$ be the one-dimensional left module defined by $\varepsilon$. Then $K_\varepsilon$ is projective if and only if there exists a nonzero idempotent $e\in A$ with $d_i e=0$ for every $1\le i<n$. Every such idempotent automatically satisfies $\varepsilon(e)=1$.
lem-temperley-lieb-quantum-binomial-digi:
## Statement

For $0\le k\le n$, let $G_{n,k}(Q)$ be the polynomial $\sum_w Q^{\operatorname{inv}(w)}$, summed over binary words with $k$ ones and $n-k$ zeros, where $\operatorname{inv}(w)$ counts pairs with a one to the left of a zero. There is a unique polynomial $B_{n,k}(T)\in\mathbb Z[T]$ such that

$$B_{n,k}(q+q^{-1})=q^{-k(n-k)}G_{n,k}(q^2).$$

It agrees as a rational-function identity with $[n]!/([k]![n-k]!)$; its value at a specialized loop parameter is the polynomial value, without division by vanishing factorials.

For a field $K$, $\delta\in K$, recurrence quantum characteristic $\ell$, and $p=\operatorname{char}K$, every $B_{n,k}(\delta)$ for $0\le k\le n$ is nonzero exactly as follows: if $\ell=\infty$, at every finite $n$; if $\ell<\infty$ and $p>0$, when $n<\ell$ or $n=a\ell p^{i-1}-1$ with $i\ge1$ and $1\le a<p$; if $\ell<\infty$ and $p=0$, when $n<\ell$ or $n=a\ell-1$ for a positive integer $a$.
lem-temperley-lieb-integral-spin-represe:
## Statement

Put $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and $\delta=q+q^{-1}$. For a commutative $A$-algebra $R$, let $V_n$ be the free $R$-module on binary words of length $n$, with $V_0=R$. The cup and cap maps are

$$c(1)=q(01)+(10),\qquad b(01)=1,\quad b(10)=q^{-1},\quad b(00)=b(11)=0.$$

Insertion of these maps in adjacent positions defines a representation

$$\rho_n:\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_R(V_n).$$

Over $A$ this map has an $A$-linear left inverse, and the same left inverse works after every base change to $R$. In particular, it is injective over every such $R$. It preserves the number of ones, and on the local ordered basis $00,01,10,11$ the generator $d_i$ has zero $00,11$ blocks and middle block

$$\begin{pmatrix}q&1\\1&q^{-1}\end{pmatrix}.$$

Horizontal reflection of an endomorphism diagram is represented by matrix transpose.
lem-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-quantum-b:
## Statement

Let $K$ be a field, $\delta\in K$, and $n\ge0$. A normalized idempotent $e\in\mathrm{TL}_n(K,\delta)$ with $d_ie=0$ for $1\le i<n$ exists if and only if every $B_{n,k}(\delta)$ of [[lem-temperley-lieb-quantum-binomial-digit-criterion]], $0\le k\le n$, is nonzero. Every such $e$ also satisfies $ed_i=0$ and is unique. This is a field assertion; it makes no integral-ring descent claim.
